title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:moment-order}
Let \(z>0\), \(\nu\geq1\), and \(A>0\) be fixed. Uniformly for
\(x\geq3\) and nonzero integers \(a\) with \(|a|\leq x^A\),
\[
 \prod_{p\mid a}\left(1+\frac{z\mathfrak s(\nu)}p\right)^{-1}
 \ll \frac{1}{x(\log x)^{z\mathfrak s(\nu)-1}}
 \sum_{n\leq x}z^{\omega(n)}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
 \ll 1,
\]
where the first implied constant depends only on \(A,z,\nu\), and
the second only on \(z,\nu\). The upper bound holds for every
nonzero integer \(a\), without the restriction \(|a|\leq x^A\).

\label{cor:Kl-large-value-concentration}
Let \(a\ne0\) and \(B\geq0\) be fixed. For every fixed
\(0<\delta<\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\), as \(x\to\infty\),
\[
 \mathbb P_x\!\left(
 \left.
 \left|\frac{\omega(n)}{\log\log x}-\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\right|
 \geq\delta\ \right|\ \mathcal L_{a,B}(x)\right)
 \ll_{a,B,\delta} (\log x)^{-\frac{\delta^2}{8\mathfrak s(\nu_B)}}.
\]
Thus \(\omega(n)/\log\log x\) converges in probability to
\(\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\) under the conditional law
\(\mathbb P_x(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal L_{a,B}(x))\).

label: lem:lambda
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Averaging \eqref{eq:prime-power-Kl-bound} over the reduced residue
  classes proves \eqref{eq:lambda-power}.

  The upper bound \eqref{eq:lambda-prime-upper} follows from
  \eqref{eq:lambda-prime} when \(p\nmid2a\). If \(p\mid a\), then
  \(\operatorname{Kl}(a\bar h^2;p)=-p^{-1/2}\) for \(h\in\mathbb F_p^\times\), so
  \(\lambda_{a,\nu}(p)=p^{-\nu/2}\). For \(\nu>0\), this is at most
  \(\mathfrak s(\nu)\) for all sufficiently large \(p\); the finitely many
  remaining primes are absorbed in the error constant. The case
  \(\nu=0\) is exact, and \(p=2\) is covered by
  \eqref{eq:lambda-power}.

  It remains to prove \eqref{eq:lambda-prime}. Suppose that
  \(p\nmid2a\). By \eqref{eq:prime-power-Kl-bound}, we may write
  \[
  \operatorname{Kl}(t;p)=2\cos\theta_{p,t},
  \qquad
  \theta_{p,t}\in[0,\pi]
  \qquad(t\in\mathbb F_p^\times).
  \]
  For \(r\geq0\), put
  \[
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta)=\frac{\sin((r+1)\theta)}{\sin\theta}.
  \]

  For \(r\geq1\), Katz \cite[Example~13.6]{Katz-1988} proved
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:full-symmetric-power}
   \bigg|\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
   \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,t})\bigg|
   \leq \frac12(r+1)p^{1/2}.
  \end{equation}
  Fouvry and Michel \cite[Lemma~2.1]{FM-2003} established the corresponding
  estimate for square parameters
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:square-symmetric-power}
   \bigg|\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
   \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,\bar h^{2}})\bigg|
   \leq 3(r+1)p^{1/2}.
  \end{equation}

  If \(a\) is a quadratic residue modulo \(p\), multiplication by
  \(a\) permutes the nonzero quadratic residues. Thus
  \[
  \sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,a\bar h^{2}})
  =\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,\bar h^{2}}).
  \]
  Otherwise, \(h\mapsto\bar h^2\) and \(h\mapsto a\bar h^2\) are
  two-to-one maps onto the nonzero quadratic residues and nonresidues,
  respectively.
  Hence
  \[
  \sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,a\bar h^{2}})
  +\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,\bar h^{2}})
  =
  2 \sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
  \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,t}).
  \]
  It follows from \eqref{eq:full-symmetric-power} and
  \eqref{eq:square-symmetric-power} that, in either case,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:a-symmetric-power}
  \begin{aligned}
   \bigg|\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
   \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,a\bar h^{2}})\bigg|
   &\leq \bigg|\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
   \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,\bar h^{2}})\bigg|
   +2\bigg|\sum_{t\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
   \operatorname{sym}_r(\theta_{p,t})\bigg|\\
   &\leq 4(r+1)p^{1/2},
  \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  uniformly in \(a\in\mathbb F_p^\times\). The argument of
  \cite[Lemmas~2.2 and 2.3]{FM-2003}, together with
  \eqref{eq:a-symmetric-power}, implies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:a-ST-discrepancy}
    \sup_{0\leq u<v\leq\pi}
    \left|
    \frac1{p-1}
    \#\left\{
    h\in\mathbb F_p^\times:
    u\leq\theta_{p,a\bar h^{2}}\leq v
    \right\}
    -
    \frac2\pi\int_u^v\sin^2t\,dt
    \right|
    \ll p^{-1/8},
  \end{equation}
  uniformly in \(a\in\mathbb F_p^\times\), with an absolute implied constant.

  For \(0\leq t\leq\pi\), put
  \[
  F_{p,a}(t)=\frac1{p-1}
  \#\{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times:\theta_{p,a\bar h^2}\leq t\}.
  \]
  For fixed \(\nu>0\), integration by parts and
  \eqref{eq:a-ST-discrepancy} imply
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
    \frac1{p-1}\sum_{h\in\mathbb F_p^\times}
    |2\cos\theta_{p,a\bar h^2}|^\nu
    &=\int_0^\pi |2\cos t|^\nu\,dF_{p,a}(t)\\
    &=\frac2\pi\int_0^\pi |2\cos t|^\nu\sin^2t\,dt
    +O_\nu(p^{-1/8})\\
    &=\mathfrak s(\nu)+O_\nu(p^{-1/8}).
  \end{aligned}
  \]
  This proves \eqref{eq:lambda-prime} and completes the proof.

label: lem:lifting
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an integer \(u\) with \(p\nmid u\). The polynomials
\(R(X)-p^\ell u\) and \(R(X)\) have the same reduction modulo \(p\), and hence share the same roots mod $p$ 
which are all simple by the hypothesis
\(p\nmid\operatorname{lc}(R)\operatorname{Disc}(R)\). By Hensel's lemma, each of these
\(\rho_R(p)\) roots, say $r$, lifts uniquely to a solution of
\(R(r)\equiv p^\ell u\,(\text{mod}\,p^{2\ell})\). Thus
\[
 \#\{r\bmod p^{2\ell}:R(r)\equiv p^\ell u\,(\text{mod}\,p^{2\ell})\}
 =\rho_R(p).
\]
Since \(p\nmid u\), the congruence \(R(r)\equiv p^\ell u\,(\text{mod}\,p^{2\ell})\) is equivalent to
\(p^\ell\parallel R(r)\) together with
\(R(r)/p^\ell\equiv u\,(\text{mod}\,p^\ell)\). For the same reason as in \eqref{p-property}, we rewrite the summation over
\(u\bmod p^\ell\) with \(p\nmid u\) to get
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\substack{r\bmod p^{2\ell}\\p^\ell\parallel R(r)}}
 \left|\operatorname{Kl}\left(a\,\overline{R(r)/p^\ell}^{\,2};p^\ell\right)\right|^\nu
 &=\rho_R(p)\sideset{}{^*}\sum_{u\bmod p^\ell}
   |\operatorname{Kl}(a\bar u^{\,2};p^\ell)|^\nu\\
 &=\rho_R(p)\varphi(p^\ell)\lambda_{a,\nu}(p^\ell),
\end{aligned}
\]
by \eqref{eq:lambda}.

label: lem:H-properties
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that \((d_1\cdots d_k,e_1\cdots e_k)=1\). Then
\[
L(\mathbf d\mathbf e)=L(\mathbf d)L(\mathbf e),
\qquad (L(\mathbf d),L(\mathbf e))=1.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d\mathbf e,r)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,r)
\ \land\
\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf e,r).
\]
Hence, by the Chinese remainder theorem, the admissible residue classes modulo
\(L(\mathbf d\mathbf e)\) are in bijection with pairs of admissible residue
classes modulo \(L(\mathbf d)\) and \(L(\mathbf e)\). We can thus split the summation in \eqref{def-H} for \(H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf{de})\).


For \(p\mid d_1\cdots d_k\), we have
\(v_p(d_je_j)=v_p(d_j)\) for \(1\leq j\leq k\).
For an admissible class $r \bmod L(\mathbf{de})$, \(Q_j(r)/d_j=e_jQ_j(r)/(d_je_j)\), so
\[
 \overline{Q_j(r)/(d_je_j)}^{\,2}\bar e_j^{\,2}
 \equiv \overline{Q_j(r)/d_j}^{\,2}\,(\text{mod}\,d_j).
\]
The analogous
argument holds when \(\mathbf d\) and \(\mathbf e\) are interchanged.
Therefore, the twisted
multiplicativity formula \eqref{eq:Kl-mult} gives
\[
 \operatorname{Kl}\!\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(r)/(d_je_j)}^{\,2};d_je_j\right)
 =
 \operatorname{Kl}\!\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(r)/d_j}^{\,2};d_j\right)
 \operatorname{Kl}\!\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(r)/e_j}^{\,2};e_j\right).
\]
The factors on the right depend only on \(r\bmod L(\mathbf d)\)
and \(r\bmod L(\mathbf e)\), respectively. We can then conclude that \(H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d\mathbf e)=     
H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d)H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf e)\)
if  \((d_1\cdots d_k, e_1\cdots e_k)=1\).




For \eqref{eq:H-comparison}, the bound \eqref{eq:Kl-Weil} implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \prod_{j=1}^k
\left|\operatorname{Kl}\!\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(r)/d_j}^{\,2};d_j\right)\right|^{\nu_j}
& \leq \prod_{j=1}^k \big(2^{\omega(d_j)}\kappa(v_2(d_j))\big)^{\nu_j},  
\end{aligned}
\]
and thus
\begin{align}\label{eq0}
\frac{ H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d)}{\prod_{j=1}^k \big(2^{\omega(d_j)}\kappa(v_2(d_j))\big)^{\nu_j}}
 &\le
 \frac{\#\{r\bmod L(\mathbf d):\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,r)\}}
      {L(\mathbf d)}.
\end{align}
As \(L(\mathbf d)| (d_1\cdots d_k)^2\),  the densities of admissible residues classes modulo \(L(\mathbf d)\) and \((d_1\cdots d_k)^2\) are the same. For an admissible class $r$, we have \(d_j\mid Q_j(r)\) for \(1\leq j\leq k\), so \(d_1\cdots d_k\mid Q(r)\). Altogether, we infer that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{\#\{r\bmod L(\mathbf d):\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,r)\}}
      {L(\mathbf d)}
 &=\frac{\#\{r\bmod(d_1\cdots d_k)^2:
                \mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,r)\}}
           {(d_1\cdots d_k)^2}\\
 &\leq\frac{\#\{r\bmod(d_1\cdots d_k)^2:
                   d_1\cdots d_k\mid Q(r)\}}
              {(d_1\cdots d_k)^2}\\
 &=\frac{\rho(d_1\cdots d_k)}{d_1\cdots d_k}.
\end{aligned}
\]
With  \eqref{eq0} and the definition of $\kappa(\cdot)$ (under  
\eqref{eq:Kl-Weil}), our assertion \eqref{eq:H-comparison} follows readily.

label: lem:local-majorant
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose \(\ell_i,\ell_j\ge 1\) for
  \(i\ne j\). Write  \(p^{\boldsymbol\ell} = (p^{\ell_1},\ldots,p^{\ell_k})\). The condition
  \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(p^{\boldsymbol\ell},r)\) would
  require \(p^{\ell_i}\mid Q_i(r)\) and \(p^{\ell_j}\mid Q_j(r)\), so \(Q_i\) and \(Q_j\) have a common root mod \(p\), as $p\nmid D$.  This contradicts (2) above. 
  Hence \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(p^{\boldsymbol\ell},r)\) does not hold for any \(r\),  implying \(H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})=0\). 
  
  Using the multiplicativity shown in Lemma~\ref{lem:H-properties},  \( H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d)\) decomposes into   
  \[H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d)= \prod_p H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(p^{{\boldsymbol\ell}_p})\]
  for some ${\boldsymbol\ell}_p\in \mathbb N_0^k$. If $(d_i,d_j)>1$ for some $i\neq j$, then some of $H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(p^{{\boldsymbol\ell}_p})$'s vanish.  The two equalities in \eqref{eq:H-majorant-coprime-D} follow from the multiplicativity, and we need to note the use of $(d_i,d_j)=1$ for all $i\neq j$ in the first equality.  
 

  Suppose that \(\ell_j=\ell\geq1\) and \(\ell_i=0\) for \(i\ne j\).
  The condition \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(p^{\boldsymbol\ell},r)\)
  then reduces to \(p^\ell\parallel Q_j(r)\) and \(p\nmid Q_i(r)\) for \(i\ne j\).  Moreover, by (1), the roots of \(Q_j\) modulo \(p\) are simple, thus by Hensel's lemma, \(\rho_{Q_j}(p^\ell)=\rho_{Q_j}(p)\).
  When \(p\nmid\operatorname{lc}(Q)\) as well, 
  \(p\nmid\operatorname{lc}(Q_j)\operatorname{Disc}(Q_j)\) and so  Lemma~\ref{lem:lifting} applies. We therefore infer that 
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
    H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(1,\ldots,p^\ell,\ldots,1)
    &=\frac1{p^{2\ell}}
      \sum_{\substack{r\bmod p^{2\ell}\\p^\ell\parallel Q_j(r)}}
      \left|\operatorname{Kl}\!\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(r)/p^\ell}^{\,2};p^\ell\right)\right|^{\nu_j}\\
    &=\rho_{Q_j}(p) \frac{\varphi(p^\ell)\lambda_{a,\nu_j}(p^\ell)}{p^{2\ell}}.
  \end{aligned}
  \]
  This proves \eqref{eq:H-good}.

label: lem:T-Delta
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(T(\mathbf d):=T_{a,\nu,F}(\mathbf d)\).
The facts that  \(T(\mathbf1_k)=1\) and 
\[ T(\mathbf a\mathbf b)\leq T(\mathbf a)T(\mathbf b) \quad \mbox{ for \((a_1\cdots a_k,b_1\cdots b_k)=1\)}
\] 
follow from  \eqref{submultiplicativity} and the multiplicativity of  \(H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}\).
This justifies the submultiplicativity of \(T\).

For \(|\boldsymbol\ell|=u\geq1\),  \eqref{eq:standard-majorant-bound} and \eqref{eq:H-fair-2}
 imply
\[
 T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})
 \ll \eta_2(p)^{|\boldsymbol\nu|}\min(A^u,Bp^{\varepsilon u})\frac{\rho(p^u)}{p^u}.
\]
Using \(\rho(p^u)\leq p^{u-1}\rho(p)\leq gp^{u-1}\) and
Stewart's estimate \eqref{eq:Stewart}, we get
\begin{align}\label{eq:se}
 T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})
 \ll_{g} \eta_2(p)^{|\boldsymbol\nu|}
 \min(A^u,Bp^{\varepsilon u})\min(p^{-1},p^{-u/g}).    
\end{align}
There are \(\binom{u+k-1}{k-1}\) vectors
\(\boldsymbol\ell\) with \(|\boldsymbol\ell|=u\).
For \(1\leq u<4g\), the factor \(A^u\) is bounded in terms of
\(A,g\). For \(u\geq4g\), the assumption
\(\varepsilon\leq1/(2g)\) and the bound
\(\binom{u+k-1}{k-1}2^{-u/(4g)}\ll_{g,k}1\) imply
\[
 \binom{u+k-1}{k-1}Bp^{-(1/g-\varepsilon)u}
 \ll_{g,k,B}p^{-u/(4g)}.
\]
Summation over \(u\geq s\) therefore proves
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{|\boldsymbol\ell|\geq s}T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})
 \ll_{g,k,A,B}\eta_2(p)^{|\boldsymbol\nu|} p^{-\max(1,s/(4g))}.
\end{equation*}

As  
\[
\Delta_p(a,\boldsymbol\nu,F) =   1+\sum_{|\boldsymbol\ell|\geq1}T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell}),
\]
we take \(s=8g\) and get from the nonnegativity of \(T\) that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta_p(a,\boldsymbol\nu,F) &= 1+ \sum_{1\leq|\boldsymbol\ell|<8g}
 T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell}) + O(p^{-2})\\
 & = \left(1+O(p^{-2})\right)
 \Big(1+\sum_{1\leq|\boldsymbol\ell|<8g}
 T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})\Big)
\end{aligned} 
\]
with nonnegative $O$-terms, where the implied $O$-constants depend on \(\boldsymbol\nu,g,k,A,B\) only. 

We apply \eqref{eq:se} to $T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})$ for $|\boldsymbol\ell|< 8g$, thus
\[
1\le  \Delta_p(a,\boldsymbol\nu,F)  = \left(1+O(p^{-2})\right)\left(1+O(p^{-1})\right)\le 1+ C p^{-1}
\]
where the constant $C>0$ depends only on \(\boldsymbol\nu,g,k,A,B\).

label: lem:polynomial-sieve
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:polynomial-sieve}
	Let \(Q\in\mathbb Z[X]\) be primitive of degree \(g\geq1\), let
	\(M\in\mathbb N\), \(r\in\mathbb Z\), and suppose that
	\[
	 x^\alpha<y\leq x,\qquad
	 M\leq x^{2\varepsilon_1},\qquad
	 2\leq z\leq x^{\varepsilon_3}.
	\]
	Then we have
	\[
		\sum_{\substack{\ x<n\leq x+y\\
				n\equiv r\,({\rm mod}\,M)\\
				p\mid Q(n),\ p\nmid M\ \Longrightarrow\ p>z}}
		1
		\ll
		\frac yM\prod_{\substack{g<p\leq z\\p\nmid M}}
		\left(1-\frac{\rho_Q(p)}p\right),
	\]
	where the implied constant depends only on \(g\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(\rho=\rho_Q\) and \(n=Mm+r\). The interval for \(m\) is
\[
 I=\left(\frac{x-r}{M},\frac{x+y-r}{M}\right],\qquad
 X=|I|=\frac yM>x^{\alpha-2\varepsilon_1}=x^{19\alpha/25}.
\]
The case \(z\leq g\) follows from
\(\#(I\cap\mathbb Z)\leq X+1\). We may thus suppose that \(z>g\), and define
\[
 \mathfrak P_g=\prod_{\substack{g<p\leq z\\p\nmid M}}p.
\]
The sum in the lemma does not exceed
\[
 \#\{m\in I\cap\mathbb Z:(Q(Mm+r),\mathfrak P_g)=1\}.
\]

For \(d\mid\mathfrak P_g\), the congruence \(Q(Mm+r)\equiv0\, (\text{mod}\,d)\) has \(\rho(d)\) solutions modulo \(d\), since \((d,M)=1\). Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sieve-remainder}
 \#\{m\in I\cap\mathbb Z:d\mid Q(Mm+r)\}
 =X\frac{\rho(d)}d+R_d,
 \qquad |R_d|\leq\rho(d).
\end{equation}

Since \(\rho(p)\leq g\), we have 
\[
 \left(1-\frac{\rho(p)}p\right)^{-1}
 \leq\left(1-\frac1p\right)^{-g}
       \bigl(1+O_g(p^{-2})\bigr)
       \quad \mbox{for \(p>2g\)},
\]
or  \(\le g+1\) for \(g<p\leq2g\).
It follows by Mertens' theorem that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sieve-dimension-axiom}
 \prod_{\substack{w\leq p<v\\p>g,\ p\nmid M}}
 \left(1-\frac{\rho(p)}p\right)^{-1}
 \ll_g\left(\frac{\log v}{\log w}\right)^g
 \qquad(2\leq w<v),
\end{equation}


We take \(D_0=z^{20g}\). Since \(\log D_0/\log z=20g>9g+1\),
the upper bound in
\cite[Corollary~6.2]{IK-2004}, together with
\eqref{eq:sieve-remainder} and \eqref{eq:sieve-dimension-axiom}, yields
\[
 \#\{m\in I\cap\mathbb Z:(Q(Mm+r),\mathfrak P_g)=1\}
 \ll_g X  \prod_{\substack{g<p\leq z\\p\nmid M}}
 \left(1-\frac{\rho(p)}p\right)
 +\sum_{\substack{d\leq D_0\\d\mid\mathfrak P_g}} \rho(d).
\]
Since \(d\mid\mathfrak P_g\) is squarefree, we have
\(\rho(d)=\prod_{p\mid d}\rho(p)\leq g^{\omega(d)}\). Hence, we get
\[
 \sum_{\substack{d\leq D_0\\d\mid\mathfrak P_g}}\rho(d)
 \leq\sum_{d\leq D_0}g^{\omega(d)}
 \ll_g D_0(\log D_0)^{g-1}.
\]
Since \(X>x^{19\alpha/25}\geq z^{38g}\) and \(D_0=z^{20g}\),
it follows from \eqref{eq:sieve-dimension-axiom} that
\[
 X\prod_{\substack{g<p\leq z\\p\nmid M}}
 \left(1-\frac{\rho(p)}p\right)
 \gg_g X(\log z)^{-g}
 \gg_g D_0(\log D_0)^{g-1}.
\]
This proves the lemma.

powers of Kloosterman sums depend only on \(n\bmod L\).
Since \(\operatorname{rad} L=\operatorname{rad}(d_1\cdots d_k)\) and \(\operatorname{rad} M=\operatorname{rad}(qd_1\cdots d_k)\), we decompose the sum into

 \sum_{\substack{t\bmod M\\

Lemma~\ref{lem:polynomial-sieve} with \(z=q\) shows that the inner sum is
\[
 \ll_g\frac yM
 \prod_{\substack{g<p\leq q\\p\nmid M}}
 \left(1-\frac{\rho(p)}p\right).
\]
Fix \(u\bmod L\) for which \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,u)\) holds.

\(\rho(q^r)\) residue classes \(t\bmod M\) satisfying
\(t\equiv u\,(\text{mod}\,L)\) and \(q^r\mid Q(t)\). Moreover, \eqref{p-property} holds for $(r,r')=(t,n)$, thus

 \frac1M
 \sum_{\substack{t\bmod M\\
                  \mathcal P_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf d,t)\\

 \prod_{j=1}^k
 \left|\operatorname{Kl}\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(t)/d_j}^{\,2};d_j\right)\right|^{\nu_j}

 \left|\operatorname{Kl}\left(a\,\overline{Q_j(u)/d_j}^{\,2};d_j\right)\right|^{\nu_j}
 \\
 &\qquad=\frac{\rho(q^r)}{q^r}H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d).

body_md:
\label{lem:stability}
Let \(F\in\mathcal M_k(A,B,\varepsilon)\), where
\(0<\varepsilon\leq1/(2g)\), and define
\[
 W(\mathbf d)=F(\mathbf d)H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d).
\]
Then the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If \(\theta:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) is multiplicative and
      \(\theta(p^\ell)=1+O(p^{-1})\) uniformly in \(p\) and
      \(\ell\geq1\), then
      \[
      \sum_{d_1\cdots d_k\leq z}W(\mathbf d)\theta(d_1\cdots d_k)
      \ll\sum_{d_1\cdots d_k\leq z}W(\mathbf d)
      \qquad(z\geq1).
      \]
      The same estimate holds with both summation ranges replaced by
      \(P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z\).
\item If \(\theta\) is as in \textup{(i)}, \(\chi>0\),
      \(z\geq\mathrm e^{8g\chi}\), and \(\sigma=\chi/\log z\), then
      \[
      \sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}
      W(\mathbf d)\theta(d_1\cdots d_k)(d_1\cdots d_k)^\sigma
      \ll\sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}W(\mathbf d).
      \]
\item For \(z\geq1\),
      \[
      \sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}W(\mathbf d)
      \asymp\sum_{d_1\cdots d_k\leq z}W(\mathbf d).
      \]
\end{enumerate}
The implied constants depend only on \(\boldsymbol\nu,g,k,A,B\), and in
\textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} also on the uniform constant in the
hypothesis on \(\theta\). The constant in \textup{(ii)} may
additionally depend on \(\chi\).

label: eq:weighted-submultiplicativity
title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(T(\mathbf d)=G_F(\mathbf d)H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}(\mathbf d)\).
Suppose that \((a_1\cdots a_k,b_1\cdots b_k)=1\). By 
\eqref{submultiplicativity} and the multiplicativity of  \(H_{a,\boldsymbol\nu}\), we have 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-submultiplicativity}
 W(\mathbf a\mathbf b)\leq T(\mathbf a)W(\mathbf b).
\end{equation}
We also have \(W\leq T\) and \(W(\mathbf1_k)=T(\mathbf1_k)=1\).

Our assertion (i) is a close analogue of \cite[Lemma~2]{Henriot-2012}, whose proof and its correction in \cite[p.~376]{Henriot-2014-erratum} rely only on inequalities as in 
\eqref{eq:weighted-submultiplicativity} and \eqref{eq:moderate}.
Therefore we can prove \textup{(i)} using the argument in \cite{Henriot-2012}. 
The summations with ranges over  \(P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z\) remain convergent because
\[
 \sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}W(\mathbf d)
 \leq\prod_{p\leq z}\bigg(1+
       \sum_{\boldsymbol\ell\ne\mathbf0}T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})\bigg)
 <\infty
\]
by \eqref{eq:moderate}.   
 These summations supported on  
\(P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z\) can be handled in the same fashion since they are dominated by the same Euler products over \(p\leq z\).
By Lemma~\ref{lem:T-Delta} (1), we see that 
 the sums over integers with bounded prime factors
converge, 



For \textup{(ii)}, the inequalities in \eqref{eq:weighted-submultiplicativity}
remain valid after multiplying \((d_1\cdots d_k)^\sigma\) to \(W(\mathbf d)\) and \(T(\mathbf d)\). Since \(\theta(p^\ell)\ll1\)
uniformly for \(\ell\geq1\), we also have
\[
 \sum_{|\boldsymbol\ell|\geq s}
 T(p^{\boldsymbol\ell})\theta(p^{|\boldsymbol\ell|})
 \ll p^{-\max(1,s/(4g))}
 \qquad(s\geq1).
\]
To apply the corrected proof of \cite[Lemma~3]{Henriot-2012},
we note that the hypothesis on \(z\) ensures
\(\sigma\leq1/(8g)\), and hence
\[
 \sum_{s>8g}p^{(\sigma-1/(4g))s}
 \ll_g p^{-1-1/(8g)}.
\]
Thus the contribution from \(s>8g\) is summable over the primes.
The corrected argument and \textup{(i)} therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}
 W(\mathbf d)\theta(d_1\cdots d_k)(d_1\cdots d_k)^\sigma\\
 &\qquad\ll\sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}
 W(\mathbf d)\theta(d_1\cdots d_k)
 \ll\sum_{P^+(d_1\cdots d_k)\leq z}W(\mathbf d).
\end{aligned}
\]

Finally, we apply the argument of \cite[Lemma~5]{Henriot-2012} and \textup{(ii)} with \(\theta=1\), \(\chi=1\) and the normalization \(W(\mathbf1_k)=1\) to derive
\textup{(iii)}, based on the same spirit that the counterparts of \eqref{eq:weighted-submultiplicativity} and \eqref{eq:moderate} are the only concerned ingredients for the proof of \cite[Lemma~4]{Henriot-2012}.

The dependency of the implied constants is clear from the arguments of our proof.

We use the argument of Nair and Tenenbaum
\cite[Section~9]{NT-1998}. Define
\(\chi_x(n)=\mathbf1_{P^-(n)>x}\) and
\(F_0(\mathbf d,d_{k+1})=F(\mathbf d)\chi_x(d_{k+1})\). One has \(F_0\in\mathcal M_{k+1}(A,B,\varepsilon)\). We set

Since \(Q(0)\ne0\), the polynomials in \(\widehat{\mathbf Q}\) are pairwise coprime and irreducible.
Moreover, \(\widehat Q\) is primitive with
\(\deg\widehat Q=g+1\) and \(\|\widehat Q\|=\|Q\|\). Thus
\eqref{eq:prime-epsilon-range} permits an application of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} to the enlarged tuple.

For \(x<n\leq x+y\leq2x\), we have \(\chi_x(n)=1\) precisely when \(n\) is prime. Applying
                       
Corollary~\ref{cor:Henriot-cor2}, the sum on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:prime-variable} is at most

 \Delta_S(a,\boldsymbol\nu,F_0)\,y

  \prod_{\substack{p\le x\\p\nmid S}}
 \left(
 1+
 \sum_{j=1}^{k+1}
 \widehat{G}_{F_0}(\mathbf p_j^1)
 \frac{\rho_{Q_j}(p)
       \lambda_{a,\nu_j}(p)}{p}
 \right)

Let \(\Theta_a\) be the sum in \eqref{eq:lower-total-weight} with the
additional factor \(\log p_1\). Since
\(\Theta_a\leq(\log x)\mathcal T_a\), it suffices, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-small-mass}, to prove
\(\Theta_a\gg_{z,\nu}x\mathcal H_a\).

Fix \(p_2,p_3\) and \(d\in\mathcal D\). The primes \(p_1\) in
\eqref{eq:lower-total-weight} are coprime to \(d\). Splitting the sum
over \(p_1\) into reduced residue classes modulo \(d\), we rewrite the inner sum of \(\Theta_a\) into
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\frac{x}{2}<dp_1p_2p_3\leq x}(\log p_1)W_d(p_1p_2p_3)
 &=\sideset{}{^*}\sum_{r\bmod d}W_d(rp_2p_3)
   \sum_{\substack{x/2<dp_1p_2p_3\leq x\\
                   p_1\equiv r\,({\rm mod}\,d)}}\log p_1\\
 &=\frac{x}{2dp_2p_3}\,z^{\omega(d)}\lambda_{a,\nu}(d)
   +E(d;p_2,p_3),
\end{aligned}
\]
by \eqref{eq:lower-small-mean} and \((p_2p_3,d)=1\), where 
\[
 E(d;p_2,p_3)=
 \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{r\bmod d}W_d(rp_2p_3)
 \left(
 \sum_{\substack{x/2<dp_1p_2p_3\leq x\\
                 p_1\equiv r \,({\rm mod}\, d)}}\log p_1
 -\frac{x}{2dp_2p_3\varphi(d)}
 \right).
\]
Using \eqref{eq:lower-weight-bound}, we get
\[
 E(d;p_2,p_3)\ll (\log x)^{B_0}\varphi(d) \max_{(r,d)=1} \max_{y\leq x/(dp_2p_3)}\bigg| \sum_{\substack{p\leq y\\
 		p \equiv r \,({\rm mod}\, d)}}\log p
 -\frac{y}{\varphi(d)}\bigg|.
\]

To sum these errors, we partition \(d\leq x^{1/30}\) into dyadic blocks
\(D\leq d<2D\). By \eqref{eq:lower-large-ranges} and \(1\leq D\leq x^{1/30}\),
we have \(16x^{1/3}<x/(Dp_2p_3) \leq x^{9/20}\).
The Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem \cite[Chapter~17]{IK-2004} therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
	 \sum_{d\in\mathcal D}|E(d;p_2,p_3)|& \ll (\log x)^{B_0+1} \max_{D\leq x^{\frac{1}{30}}} D  \sum_{\substack{d\in\mathcal D\\D\leq d<2D}} \max_{(r,d)=1} \max_{y\leq x/(Dp_2p_3)}\bigg| \sum_{\substack{p\leq y\\
	 		p \equiv r \,({\rm mod}\, d)}}\log p
	 -\frac{y}{\varphi(d)}\bigg|\\
& \ll \frac{x}{p_2p_3(\log x)^{2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Recall that  \(\Theta_a\) is defined as in \eqref{eq:lower-total-weight} with $W_d(p_1p_2p_3)\log p_1$ in place of $W_d(p_1p_2p_3)$. It follows from Mertens' estimate that the contribution from $E(d;p_2,p_3)$ to  $ \Theta_a$ is $O(x/(\log x)^{2})$.
We therefore conclude that
\[
 \Theta_a=
 \frac{x}{2}\left(\sum_{p_2}\frac{1}{p_2}\right)
          \left(\sum_{p_3}\frac{1}{p_3}\right)\mathcal H_a
 +O_{z,\nu}\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^2}\right).
\]
Since \(\mathcal H_a\geq1\), the $O_{z,\nu}$-term  is
\(o(x\mathcal H_a)\). Thus \(\Theta_a\gg_{z,\nu}x\mathcal H_a\),
as required.

       \left(\frac NP+P\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\Big(\sum_m|f(m)|^2\Big) ^{\frac{1}{2}}\right),
\end{aligned}
\]

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lower-large-prime-ST}

\[
 \mathcal T_{a,j}(I)
 =\mu_{\rm ST}(I)\mathcal T_a^\ast+o(\mathcal T_a^\ast),

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(j\in\{1,2,3\}\). Throughout the proof, \(p_2,p_3\)
satisfy \eqref{eq:lower-large-ranges}, \(p_1\) satisfies
\eqref{eq:lower-p1-range}, and \(p_i\nmid2a\) for
\(1\leq i\leq3\). These three intervals are disjoint and lie
above \(Z\).

For each \(d\in\mathcal D\), we split the sum over \(p_j\) in
\(\mathcal T_{a,j}(I)\) into \(O(\log x)\) dyadic intervals \([P,2P)\) and reduced residue
classes modulo \(d\). Fix \(P\) and a reduced residue class
\(b\bmod d\), and let \(\mathcal P\) denote the corresponding
set of primes. Here \(x^{1/4}\ll P\ll x^{9/20}\) and
\(d\leq x^{1/30}\). For the application of Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-large-sieve}, define
\[
f(m)=
\begin{cases}
	W_d\!\left(\frac{bm}{d}\right),
	&\displaystyle m=d\prod_{i\ne j}p_i\leq\frac{x}{P},\\[2mm]
	0,&\text{otherwise}
\end{cases}.
\]
We use the unique representation $m=dp_1p_2p_3$. For
\(m\) in the support of \(f\) and \(p\in\mathcal P\), we have
\((m/d,d)=(m,p)=1\). Since \(p\equiv b\pmod d\), the
periodicity of \(W_d\) yields
\[
f(m)=W_d\!\left(\frac{bm}{d}\right)
=W_d\!\left(\frac{pm}{d}\right)
=W_d(p_1p_2p_3),
\qquad p_j=p.
\]
Thus, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-angle-decomposition}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_{a,j}(I)
 &=\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}\sum_P
   \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{b\bmod d}
   \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}
   \sum_{\substack{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x\\
                   \theta_{p,a\bar m^2}\in I}}f(m),\\
 \mathcal T_a^\ast
 &=\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}\sum_P
   \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{b\bmod d}
   \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}
   \sum_{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x}f(m).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal P\) and \(f\) depend on \(d,P,b\).

We obtain from \eqref{eq:lower-weight-bound} that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:second-f}
	 \sum_m|f(m)|^2
	\leq(\log x)^{2B_0}
	\sum_{\substack{m\leq\frac{x}{P}\\d\mid m}}1
	\leq\frac{x}{Pd}(\log x)^{2B_0}.
\end{equation}
With \(N=x/P\) and \(Y=x\), Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-large-sieve} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-angle-block}
	\begin{aligned}
		\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}
		\sum_{\substack{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x\\
				\theta_{p,a\bar m^2}\in I}}f(m)=&\left(\mu_{\rm ST}(I)+O(P^{-\frac{1}{8}})\right)
		\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x}f(m)
		+O\left(\frac{x^{\frac{19}{20}}(\log x)^{B_0+1}}{d}\right)\\
		=&\mu_{\rm ST}(I)\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x}f(m)
		+O\left(\frac{x^{\frac{31}{32}}(\log x)^{B_0}}{d^2}+\frac{x^{\frac{19}{20}}(\log x)^{B_0+1}}{d}\right).
	\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the error in Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-large-sieve}
is bounded by
\[
(\log x)(P\#\mathcal P)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\left(\frac{x}{P^2}+P\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\left(\sum_m|f(m)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\ll\frac{x^{\frac{19}{20}}(\log x)^{B_0+1}}{d},
\]
where we used the bound \eqref{eq:second-f}, \(\#\mathcal P\ll P/d\) and
\(x^{1/4}\ll P\ll x^{9/20}\).
By using \(d\mid m\) for $m$ on the support
of \(f\) and  \eqref{eq:lower-weight-bound}, the error term coming from \(O(P^{-1/8})\) is bounded by
\[
P^{-\frac18}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\sum_{\frac{x}{2}<pm\leq x}f(m)
\ll P^{-\frac18}\#\mathcal P\,\frac{x}{Pd}(\log x)^{B_0}
\ll\frac{x^{\frac{31}{32}}(\log x)^{B_0}}{d^2}.
\]

We now sum \eqref{eq:lower-angle-block} over \(b\), the dyadic
intervals, and \(d\in\mathcal D\). The errors contribute
\[
 \ll\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}\sum_P
       \sideset{}{^*}\sum_{b\bmod d}\left(\frac{x^{\frac{31}{32}}(\log x)^{B_0}}{d^2}+\frac{x^{\frac{19}{20}}(\log x)^{B_0+1}}{d} \right)       
 \ll x^{\frac{59}{60}}(\log x)^{B_0+2}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:lower-angle-decomposition} and \eqref{eq:T}, we obtain
\[
 \left|\mathcal T_{a,j}(I)-\mu_{\rm ST}(I)\mathcal T_a^\ast\right|
 \ll_{A,z,\nu}x^{\frac{59}{60}}(\log x)^{B_0+2}
 =o(\mathcal T_a^\ast).
\]

label: eq:upper-LaB
title: Proof
body_md:
For every \(n\in\mathcal L_{a,B}(x)\), one has
\(|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\nu_B}\geq (\log x)^{B\nu_B}\). By Corollary~\ref{cor:moment-order}, we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper-LaB}
	 \#\mathcal L_{a,B}(x)
	\leq (\log x)^{-B\nu_B}
	\sum_{x/2<n\leq x}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\nu_B}
	\ll x(\log x)^{-I(B)}.
\end{equation}


Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). For \(\tau>0\), write
\(\nu:=\nu_B+\tau\) and \(\beta:=\mathfrak s'(\nu+\tau)\). As
\(\tau\to0^+\), we have
\(1+\nu\beta-\mathfrak s(\nu)\longrightarrow I(B)\).
We may therefore choose \(\tau=\tau(B,\varepsilon)>0\) so small that
\[
 1+\nu\beta-\mathfrak s(\nu)<I(B)+\varepsilon.
\]
Since \(\mathfrak s'(\nu_B)=B\), the strict convexity of \(\mathfrak s\) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:B-beta}
 \beta>B,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathfrak s(\nu)-\mathfrak s(\nu-\tau)}{\tau}>B,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathfrak s(\nu+\tau)-\mathfrak s(\nu)}{\tau}<\beta.
\end{equation}
By Corollary~\ref{cor:moment-order} and \eqref{eq:B-beta}, there is a
constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\substack{x/2<n\leq x\\
 |\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|\notin[(\log x)^B,(\log x)^\beta]}}
 |\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
 &\leq
 (\log x)^{B\tau}\sum_{n\leq x}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\nu-\tau}
 +(\log x)^{-\beta\tau}\sum_{n\leq x}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\nu+\tau}\\
 &\ll
 x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu-\tau)-1+B\tau}
 +x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu+\tau)-1-\beta\tau}\\
 &\ll x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu)-1-c}.
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, Theorem~\ref{thm:lower}, with \(z=1\) and exponent
\(\nu\), gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{x/2<n\leq x\\n\ \mathrm{squarefree}\\(n,2a)=1}}
 |\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
 \gg x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu)-1}.
\]
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:large-value-mass}
 x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu)-1}
 \ll\sum_{\substack{x/2<n\leq x\\
                    n\ \mathrm{squarefree},\ (n,2a)=1\\
                    (\log x)^B\leq|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|\leq(\log x)^\beta}}
 |\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
 \leq(\log x)^{\nu\beta}\#\mathcal L_{a,B}(x).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower-LaB}
 \#\mathcal L_{a,B}(x)
 \gg\frac{x}{(\log x)^{1+\nu\beta-\mathfrak s(\nu)}}
 \geq\frac{x}{(\log x)^{I(B)+\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eq:upper-LaB} and \eqref{eq:lower-LaB}, we obtain
\[
 (\log x)^{-I(B)-\varepsilon}
 \ll\mathbb P_x\bigl(\mathcal L_{a,B}(x)\bigr)
 \ll(\log x)^{-I(B)}.
\]
We take logarithms and divide by \(\log\log x\), then let
\(x\to\infty\) and \(\varepsilon\to0\), in this order. This proves
the corollary.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(0<\delta<\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\). For each choice of sign, let $ z_\pm=1\pm \delta/\mathfrak s(\nu_B)$
and
\[
 E_\pm:=\left\{n\in\mathcal L_{a,B}(x):
 \pm\bigl(\omega(n)-\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\log\log x\bigr)
 \geq\delta\log\log x\right\}.
\]
Since \(z_+>1\) and \(0<z_-<1\), for either sign and every
\(n\in E_\pm\) we have
\[
 z_\pm^{\omega(n)}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\nu_B}
 \geq(\log x)^{B\nu_B+(\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\pm\delta)\log z_\pm}.
\]
The upper bound in Corollary~\ref{cor:moment-order}, together with
\(I(B)=1+B\nu_B-\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\), therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb P_x(E_\pm)
 \ll(\log x)^{-I(B)-(\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\pm\delta)\log z_\pm\mp\delta}.
 \]
The elementary inequality
\[
 (1+u)\log(1+u)-u\geq\frac{u^2}{4}
 \quad(0<|u|<1)
\]
shows that
\[
 (\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\pm\delta)\log z_\pm\mp\delta
 \geq\frac{\delta^2}{4\mathfrak s(\nu_B)}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \mathbb P_x(E_+\cup E_-)
 \ll(\log x)^{-I(B)-\frac{\delta^2}{4\mathfrak s(\nu_B)}}.
\]
On the other hand, \eqref{eq:lower-LaB} with
\(\varepsilon=\delta^2/(8\mathfrak s(\nu_B))\) gives
\[
 \mathbb P_x\bigl(\mathcal L_{a,B}(x)\bigr)
 \gg(\log x)^{-I(B)-\frac{\delta^2}{8\mathfrak s(\nu_B)}}.
\]
Dividing these estimates, we obtain
\[
 \mathbb P_x\!\left(
 \left.\left|\frac{\omega(n)}{\log\log x}-\mathfrak s(\nu_B)\right|
 \geq\delta\ \right|\ \mathcal L_{a,B}(x)\right)
 \ll_{a,B,\delta}
 (\log x)^{-\frac{\delta^2}{8\mathfrak s(\nu_B)}}.
\]

Put $F(n)=|\lambda_f(n)|^\mu$. The Hecke relations and Deligne's bound \cite{Deligne-1974} show that
\(F\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_1(A,B,\varepsilon_0)\), for suitable \(A,B\) and every
fixed \(\varepsilon_0>0\). Moreover, \(G_F=F\), and hence $ G_F(p)=|\lambda_f(p)|^\mu$.

We apply Corollary~\ref{cor:Henriot-cor2} with \(Q(X)=X\). Here
\(D=1\) and \(\rho_Q(p)=1\). Mertens' theorem and
\eqref{eq:lambda-prime-upper} yield
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cor33-45}
	\sum_{x<n\leq x+y}
	|\lambda_f(n)|^\mu|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu\ll
	\frac{y}{\log x}
	\prod_{p\leq x}
	\left(
	1+\frac{\mathfrak s(\nu)|\lambda_f(p)|^\mu}{p}
	+O_{\mu,\nu}\left(p^{-\frac98}\right)
	\right).
\end{equation}
It follows from \eqref{eq:Hecke-ST-prime} that
\[

 \left(
 1+\frac{\mathfrak s(\nu)|\lambda_f(p)|^\mu}{p}
 +O_{\mu,\nu}\left(p^{-\frac98}\right)
 \right)
 \leq

\]

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Since \(\mathfrak s(0)=1\) and \(\mathfrak s\) is
	continuous at \(0\), we may fix \(\nu>0\) such that $1+\mathfrak s(2\nu)-2\mathfrak s(\nu)<\varepsilon$.
	Denote
	\(
	\mathcal S(x)
	=\{n:x/2<n\leq x,\  \mu^2(n)=1,\ (n,2a)=1\}\) and 
	\[
	\mathcal D(x)
	=\{n\in\mathcal S(x):\lambda_f(n)\ne\pm\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)\}.
	\]
	For $n\in\mathcal S(x)\setminus\mathcal D(x)$, we have $|\lambda_f(n)|=|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|$. Thus, Corollary~\ref{cor:Hecke-Kl-mixed} yields
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:fourier-kl-nu}
		\sum_{n\in\mathcal S(x)\setminus\mathcal D(x)}
		|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu=\sum_{n\in\mathcal S(x)\setminus\mathcal D(x)}
		|\lambda_f(n)|^{\frac{\nu}{2}}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{\frac{\nu}{2}}
		\ll x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu/2)^2-1+\varepsilon'},
	\end{equation}
	where the constant $\varepsilon'>0$ is sufficiently small. On the other hand, Theorem~\ref{thm:lower} yields
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:fourier-kl-nu-2}
	\sum_{n\in\mathcal S(x)}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
	\gg x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu)-1}.
	\end{equation}
	By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, we get from \eqref{eq:sato-moment} that
	\(\mathfrak s(\nu/2)^2<\mathfrak s(\nu)\). Subtracting \eqref{eq:fourier-kl-nu} into \eqref{eq:fourier-kl-nu-2}, we obtain
   \begin{equation}\label{eq:Dset-lower}
	\sum_{n\in\mathcal D(x)}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
	\gg x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(\nu)-1}.
	\end{equation}
	We use the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality again and the upper bound in
	Corollary~\ref{cor:moment-order}, and get
	\[
	\sum_{n\in\mathcal D(x)}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^\nu
	\leq \big(\#\mathcal D(x)\big)^{\frac{1}{2}}
	\Big(\sum_{n\leq x}|\operatorname{Kl}(a;n)|^{2\nu}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}
	\ll \big(\#\mathcal D(x)\big)^{\frac{1}{2}}
	\big(x(\log x)^{\mathfrak s(2\nu)-1}\big)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
	\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:Dset-lower}, we derive
	\[
	\#\mathcal D(x)
	\gg
	\frac{x}{(\log x)^{1+\mathfrak s(2\nu)-2\mathfrak s(\nu)}}
	\gg
	\frac{x}{(\log x)^\varepsilon}.
	\]
	This completes the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:Hecke-Kl-noncoincidence}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The number variance of Li and Sarnak
\cite[Theorem~1.4]{LiSarnak-2004} admits the asymptotic formula
\begin{equation*}
	\Sigma_h(T,L)=R(T,L)+O\!\left(\frac{T}{L^2}\right)
\end{equation*}
uniformly in the range \eqref{eq:spectral-window}, where 
\[
R(T,L)=\frac{T}{\pi^6L^2}
\left(\int_0^\infty\xi^5\psi(\xi)\,d\xi\right)
\sum_{\substack{u,n\geq1\\(u,n)=1}}
\prod_{p\mid n}(1-p^{-2})^{-2}
\frac{|S(u,u;n)|^2}{u^2n^2}
\left|\widehat h\!\left(\frac{\log(Tn/u)}{\pi L}\right)\right|^2.
\]

Since \(\operatorname{supp}\widehat h\subset(-1,1)\), a nonzero
term in \(R(T,L)\) must satisfy $n<u e^{\pi L}/T \leq uT^{\frac{1}{121}}$.
Moreover, $\widehat h(\xi)\ll 1$ and $1\leq\prod_{p\mid n}(1-p^{-2})^{-2}\leq\zeta(2)^2$. Note that  \(L\asymp\log T\). Thus, the upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:LS} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:R-upperbound}
	\begin{aligned}
		R(T,L)
		&\ll\frac{T}{L^2}
		\sum_{u\geq1}\frac{1}{u^2}
		\sum_{n\leq uT^{\frac{1}{121}}}
		\frac{|S(u,u;n)|^2}{n^2}\\
		&\ll\frac{T}{L^2}
		\sum_{u\geq1}\frac{\tau(u)^2\log(uT^{\frac{1}{121}})}{u^2}
		\ll\frac{T}{L}.
	\end{aligned}
\end{equation}


For the lower bound, it is clear that
\[
R(T,L)\gg \frac{T}{L^2}
\sum_{n\geq1}
\frac{|S(1,1;n)|^2}{n^2}
\left|\widehat h\!\left(\frac{\log(Tn)}{\pi L}\right)\right|^2.
\]
By the choice of $h$, there exist $b_1,b_2$ such that \((1+\delta)^{-1}<b_1<b_2<1\) and \(|\widehat h|\gg 1\) on \([b_1,b_2]\). By partial summation and the estimate \eqref{eq:cor41-fixeda-2}, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
	R(T,L)
	&\gg \frac{T}{L^2}
	\sum_{e^{\pi Lb_1}/T<n\leq e^{\pi Lb_2}/T}
	\frac{|S(1,1;n)|^2}{n^2} \\
	&\gg \frac{T}{L^2}
	\sum_{e^{\pi Lb_1}/T<n\leq e^{\pi Lb_2}/T}
	\frac{|\operatorname{Kl}(1;n)|^2}{n} \\
	&\gg \frac{T}{L}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:R-upperbound}, we conclude
\eqref{eq:spectral-variance-order}.

To prove \eqref{eq:spectral-mean-square}, we apply \eqref{eq:spectral-variance-order} with a fixed nonnegative smooth function \(\psi\) supported in \([4/3,5/3]\), with \(\int_0^\infty\psi(x)\,dx=1\), and take
\(L=(1+\delta)\log T/\pi\). By the definition of \(N(t)\) and the evenness of \(h\), we have
\[
 N_h(t,L)
 =\int_0^\infty h(L(t-\xi))\,dN(\xi)
 =\int_0^\infty h(L(\xi-t))\,dN(\xi).
\]
By \eqref{eq:spectral-Weyl} and integration by parts, we obtain
\[
 N_h(t,L)-\frac{t}{6L}
 =-\int_0^\infty Lh'(L(\xi-t))S(\xi)\,d\xi+O(\log (1+|t|)),
\]
where we used the fact \(\int_{\mathbb R}h(x)dx=1\).  See also \cite[(6.11)]{LiSarnak-2004}. For any \(t\in[4T/3,5T/3]\), it follows from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality that
\[
 \left|N_h(t,L)-\frac{t}{6L}\right|^2
 \ll(\log T)^2+
 \int_0^\infty |Lh'(L(\xi-t))|S(\xi)^2\,d\xi.
\]
By the choice of \(\psi\), we get
\[
 T\Sigma_h(T,L)
 \ll T(\log T)^2+\int_0^\infty S(\xi)^2
 \bigg(\int_{\frac{4T}{3}}^{\frac{5T}{3}}
 |Lh'(L(\xi-t))|\,dt\bigg)d\xi.
\]
Since \(h'\) is integrable, the inner integral is at most
\(\|h'\|_1\), uniformly in \(\xi\).
For \(\xi \notin [T,2T]\), we have $ |\xi-t|\gg T+\xi$. Thus, the rapid decay of \(h'\) yields 
\[
 \int_{\frac{4T}{3}}^{\frac{5T}{3}}|Lh'(L(\xi-t))|\,dt
 \ll\frac{T}{(T+\xi)^5}
 \leq\frac{1}{(T+\xi)^4}.
\]
By \cite[(1.4)]{LiSarnak-2004}, \(S(\xi)\ll 1+\xi\). Hence the contribution
from \(\xi\notin[T,2T]\) is
\[
 \ll\int_0^\infty\frac{(1+\xi)^2}{(T+\xi)^4}\,d\xi
 \ll\frac{1}{T}.
\]
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:spectral-transfer}
 T\Sigma_h(T,L)
 \ll T(\log T)^2+\int_T^{2T}S(\xi)^2\,d\xi.
\end{equation}
The lower bound in \eqref{eq:spectral-variance-order}
shows that \(T\Sigma_h(T,L)\gg T^2/\log T\). The estimate \eqref{eq:spectral-mean-square} now follows from \eqref{eq:spectral-transfer}. The \(\Omega\)-estimate follows from
\[
 \sup_{T\leq t\leq2T}|S(t)|^2
 \geq\frac{1}{T}\int_T^{2T}S(t)^2\,dt
 \gg\frac{T}{\log T}.
\]
